research_question: Under back-to-back multi-camera handoff (N=8, K=2, burst_gap_ms=0) vs sparse bursts (burst_gap_ms=350), does pool_hybrid dominate both pool_auto_0 (eliminating the overlap peak under gap=0) and pool_coop (reclaiming idle streams under gap=350), and how do both compare against BFC, direct_malloc, and direct_jemalloc?
hypothesis: pool_hybrid achieves peak phys_footprint <= pool_coop < pool_auto_0 < pool_retain < bfc under back-to-back handoff (gap=0) while achieving mean/final phys_footprint < pool_coop under sparse bursts (gap=350), with fewer minor faults than direct_jemalloc and max_abs_error == 0.
acceptance_gates: 1) max_abs_error == 0 across all 50 runs; 2) gap=0 peak phys_footprint(pool_hybrid) < pool_auto_0 < pool_retain < bfc; 3) gap=350 mean/final phys_footprint(pool_hybrid) < pool_coop; 4) validate_run.py --require-protocol --min-trials 5 passes.
